reference: Own python implementation of the six-group point-kinetics equations using the delayed-neutron data read out of the tool itself (beta_i = 2.15e-4, 1.424e-3, 1.274e-3, 2.568e-3, 7.48e-4, 2.73e-4; lambda_i = 0.0124, 0.0305, 0.111, 0.301, 1.14, 3.01 1/s; beta = 0.006502). Three structurally independent routes are computed and cross-checked: (1) brentq root of the inhour equation rho = w*Lambda + sum beta_i w/(w+lambda_i); (2) the dominant eigenvalue of the 7x7 point-kinetics system matrix (numpy.linalg.eig); (3) a stiff integration of the full six-group ODE system (scipy solve_ivp, Radau, rtol 1e-10) checked against the exact 7-mode modal solution.  Routes (1) and (2) agree to 5e-13 relative, (3) and the modal solution to 3e-11.
reference_citations: G.R. Keepin, "Physics of Nuclear Kinetics", Addison-Wesley (1965), Table 4-6 - six-group delayed-neutron parameters for thermal fission of U-235 (the data set used by the tool).
J.J. Duderstadt and L.J. Hamilton, "Nuclear Reactor Analysis", Wiley (1976), Table 2-3 and Sec. 6.1 (point kinetics, inhour equation, prompt jump).
J.R. Lamarsh and A.J. Baratta, "Introduction to Nuclear Engineering", 3rd ed., Table 7.3 and Sec. 7.3.
tolerance: readout values: half of the last printed digit (the tool prints 4 significant digits for the period and doubling time, 3 decimals for the prompt-jump factor, integers for pcm) plus 1e-6 relative.  Plotted transient: the curve is read back off the canvas, so the pass criterion is 3 pixels of vertical resolution (stated per case in resolution.one_pixel_is_rel) or 6 %, whichever is larger.
